intro.title: Home Field
text: You've bought a field off Mill Lane, outside the village of Ashby. Under the grass there's topsoil, then clay, sand and gravel, and people pay good money for all of it.

There's $200 in the bank, a shovel, a wheelbarrow and your tired pickup. Practise by hand or try a short machine rental at Ashby Plant. The Micro 08 is a cheap first digger; bigger kit comes from selling clean loads at Ashby Aggregates.

steps.title: Dig with the shovel
steps.text: Walk onto your field (through the gap from the yard), look at the ground and click to dig a shovelful.
steps.mentor: Ray here, the one who sold you the field. First job: grab the shovel and dig. The topsoil's the good stuff, the depot pays best for it. Follow the marker onto your field.

steps.title: Fill the wheelbarrow
steps.text: The wheelbarrow is just inside the field. Look into it and click to tip each shovelful in, until it's full.
steps.mentor: Tip each shovelful into the barrow. It's just inside the field, marked for you. A full barrow's about 110 kilos.

steps.title: Load the pickup
steps.text: Your pickup is parked in the yard. Take the barrow (E), push it up to the pickup's tailgate and tip it in (T). Keep going until there's at least 300 kg on board.
steps.mentor: Wheel it up to the pickup's tailgate and tip it in. Or save your legs: park the pickup on the field and shovel straight in.

steps.title: Weigh in at the depot
steps.text: Get in the pickup (E) and drive to Ashby Aggregates: out of the gate, east along Mill Lane, north into Ashby and left at The Plough onto Quarry Road (Tab shows the map). Stop on the weighbridge at the depot gate.
steps.mentor: That'll do for a first load. Drive to Ashby Aggregates, it's on the map (Tab). Stop dead on the weighbridge at the gate and wait for the light.

steps.title: Unload in the topsoil bay
steps.text: Back up to the TOPSOIL bay and unload (T). Clean loads pay the most: mixed ones are graded down.
steps.mentor: Back up to the TOPSOIL bay and unload. Keep it clean: a load with clay mixed in gets paid less.

steps.title: Fix up the pickup
steps.text: Cheap upgrades make old machines a bit better. Stiffer rear springs let the pickup carry more: buy them in the shop (B, or the office laptop).
steps.mentor: First money in! Stiffer rear springs for the pickup are cheap and she'll carry more. Office laptop, or B anywhere.

steps.title: Buy a mini digger
steps.text: Buy one of the four compact diggers at Ashby Plant (B). The Micro 08 is the cheapest; the Mini 16 has a larger bucket and stronger hydraulics. Rentals let you try a machine first.
steps.mentor: Try a small digger next. The Micro 08 is cheap, and the Mini 16 has more muscle. Every model feels different. Rent one at the plant dealer if you want to try it first.

steps.title: Dig with the digger
steps.text: Get in the mini digger (E), drive it onto your field, swing the bucket over the ground and hold the left mouse button. Swing round and click to dump into the pickup (park it close).
steps.mentor: Get in the digger and take a bucket. Park the pickup alongside so you can swing straight into it. G swaps to Direct controls if you fancy doing it properly.

steps.title: Buy a tractor and trailer
steps.text: Buy a tractor and a separate tipping trailer in the dealer. The Yard tractor and Yard Tipper are the cheapest pair. Drive within 10 m of the trailer, stop, and hitch it in Fleet.
steps.mentor: The pickup is holding you back. Buy a tractor and its own trailer, then hitch them in Fleet. Watch the gross tow limit: the empty trailer counts too.

steps.title: Sell a trailer load
steps.text: Fill your hitched trailer with at least 1 t, drive to the depot, weigh in and tip in the right bay (T). Slow down when reversing; trailer brakes and gross weight matter.
steps.mentor: Fill your own trailer with a tonne or more, then take it over the weighbridge. Go slowly in reverse. A heavier trailer needs a stronger tractor.

steps.title: Build a ramp or a haul road
steps.text: On foot, press F to plan groundworks: a ramp out of your pit, a gravel haul road, or a level area for turning the trailer. Click the start, then the end, and click again to build. A road or ramp is surfaced with gravel from the strip and loose gravel heaps within 30 m; a level area needs none.
steps.mentor: Tractor's earning its keep. Now make the site work for you: a ramp out of the pit or a level pad saves you fighting the ground every load. Press F on foot to plan one. Nothing's spent till you click to build.

steps.title: Buy an excavator
steps.text: Choose an excavator at Ashby Plant: Utility 80 through Heavy 320 offer more reach, breakout force and bucket capacity. The cheapest production digger is the Utility 80.
steps.mentor: Now choose more digging power. The Utility 80 is a useful step up; bigger excavators reach farther and bite harder. Match the digger to the ground and your haulage.

steps.title: Buy a tipper truck
steps.text: A tipper truck is faster on the road and carries more than the starter trailer. Save up for the Rusty Tipper Truck.
steps.mentor: Next, a tipper truck. More than the starter trailer takes, and quicker on the road.

steps.title: Sell a truck load
steps.text: Load the truck with the excavator, drive it to the depot, weigh in and tip in the right bay (T).
steps.mentor: Load the truck with the excavator and take it to the depot. Same drill: weighbridge, then the right bay.

steps.title: Earn $3,000
steps.text: Keep digging, hauling and selling. Service your machines (R) before they break down. A site dumper can move material round your field while the digger keeps digging.
steps.mentor: That's a working quarry. Keep the machines serviced and the loads clean, and put money by.

steps.title: Get a better machine
steps.text: Choose another model or a second-hand upgrade. Model size, reach and force matter separately from condition.
steps.mentor: Look for a machine that suits your ground. A bigger bucket and more force make a difference; condition tells you when it needs a service.

steps.title: Supply clean material
steps.text: Sell 60 t of clean material, or complete an optional customer order from the Jobs board for a bonus.
steps.mentor: Keep the clean loads coming. Sixty tonnes builds a useful supply business. There are optional customer orders on the Jobs board if you fancy a bonus.

steps.title: Fit out the yard
steps.text: Buy a yard building in the plant dealer's Yard buildings tab: the container workshop makes servicing and repairs cheaper and quicker, the bulk fuel supply cuts your diesel bill.
steps.mentor: Your running costs are adding up. Fit out the yard: the old container makes a decent workshop, and a bulk fuel deal takes a slice off every tank. Plant dealer, Yard buildings.

steps.title: Sell 300 t of clean material
steps.text: Dig one layer at a time and keep your heaps apart: only clean loads in the right bay count. Clean loads in a row also count towards the milestones on the laptop.
steps.mentor: Clean loads pay best, and the depot remembers who sends them. Keep your layers apart and put 300 tonnes of clean stuff over their weighbridge. Your milestones are on the laptop too: plenty there worth chasing.

steps.title: Build a name in Ashby
steps.text: Sell 500 t of clean material, or reach reputation 3 by finishing optional customer orders.
steps.mentor: Clean loads earn trust. Keep supplying good material, or take an occasional customer order if you want the extra bonus.

steps.title: Build a stronger fleet
steps.text: Own a digger of at least 3.5 t and a road haulage vehicle or tractor/trailer combination carrying at least 6 t. Existing Used machines also count.
steps.mentor: Match digging to haulage: a stronger digger and a larger truck or trailer work well together. Keep the kit you use and sell what you have outgrown.

steps.title: Earn $15,000
steps.text: Keep the loads clean and the machines serviced. Watch the depot prices: news in the Prices app moves them for a few days at a time.
steps.mentor: That's a real business now. Keep an eye on the prices: when there's news, hold off on what's down and sell what's up. Fifteen grand and you can call yourself a quarry.

tips.breakdown: Broken down? Walk up to it and press R to repair. Service them before they get that bad (R when you're next to one): it's cheaper than a repair.
tips.mixedLoad: That load was graded down: it had other stuff mixed in. Dig one layer at a time and keep your heaps apart.
tips.worn: One of your machines is getting tired (under 40%). A service (R next to it) puts it right before it lets you down.
tips.broke: Money's tight. Sell a clean load before you spend on fuel and repairs. You can go into debt, but the bank charges interest.
tips.works: Now you have a machine on the field, press F to plan a gravel haul road, or a ramp out of a pit. It's built from what you dig out plus loose gravel heaps within 30 m, so tip some gravel by it first. Right click cancels; nothing is spent until you click to build.
tips.inspector: The council's inspector is coming round. They don't like broken or worn-out machines: service anything under 40% (R when you're next to it) before they get here, or it's a fine. Everything tidy and they'll put a good word in for you.
